Academic Context  
Wendy’s work at SecureNet intersected with my research on cybersecurity frameworks, where her insights into threat modeling enriched a collaborative paper on adaptive defense strategies. Her ability to synthesize technical complexity into accessible narratives made her a natural collaborator, even in brief interactions.  

Working Relationship  
We connected through a joint workshop on secure product design, where Wendy led a session on user-centric risk assessment. Her clarity in explaining trade-offs between security and usability impressed colleagues, and her follow-up emails with actionable takeaways reflected a genuine commitment to shared goals.  

Research Ability  
Wendy’s approach to UX research in SecureNet’s identity management tool showcased her knack for uncovering hidden pain points. During a stakeholder workshop, she probed beyond surface-level feedback to reveal how team workflows were disrupted by authentication delays—a finding that reshaped the product’s prioritization.  

Broader Strengths  
Beyond her technical rigor, Wendy’s curiosity drives her to ask “why” behind every decision. She once renegotiated a timeline to incorporate a less obvious security layer, arguing it would prevent downstream vulnerabilities. Her stakeholder management skills shine in balancing executive demands with engineering realities, ensuring no critical voice is sidelined.  

Recommendation  
Wendy’s blend of technical precision and collaborative empathy makes her a standout candidate. She thrives in environments where complexity meets urgency, and her dedication to solving problems through dialogue—not just data—sets her apart. I’d welcome the chance to see her contribute to your team’s mission.
